title: Leaders Who Manage Others Poorly by Email
author: Admired Leadership
summary: This piece argues email is a fundamentally poor medium for leading people, even though it excels at sharing information. Because it strips out social and nonverbal cues, email invites over-interpretation from readers and, on the writer's side, encourages a more inflammatory tone than face-to-face conversation would allow. The essay describes how leaders use email to avoid uncomfortable direct conversations — including sending emotionally charged group messages meant for one or two people — and argues that relying on email for feedback, praise, or difficult conversations degrades the connection team members need to feel valued.
points: Argues email's stripped-out nonverbal cues make it prone to over-interpretation and misread tone on the receiving end.
Notes email tends to push writers toward more inflammatory, 'drop the bomb and walk away' language than face-to-face conversation permits.
Identifies a specific failure mode: sending group emails with negative feedback meant for one or two people, leaving everyone feeling accused.
Frames over-reliance on email as a way leaders avoid the discomfort of direct, difficult conversations rather than a neutral efficiency choice.
Recommends reserving email strictly for information-sharing and announcements, not for feedback, praise, or conflict.
quotes: Because it lacks the social, visual, and nonverbal cues essential for understanding, email is often misunderstood, misinterpreted, and overanalyzed.
That’s why email is such a terrible medium through which to express anything symbolic or humanly important. It leaves way too much to chance.
Instead, the medium allows people to drop “bombs” and then walk away without needing to deal with the consequences.
In fact, it is common for those leaders reliant on email to blast out negative group messages that should have targeted one or two team members. In such cases, everyone feels accused and reprimanded.
They know that nothing can replace the impact and clarity of face-to-face interaction, and they lead accordingly.
